description: The Historical Alberta Resource Atlas is a series of page-sized maps describing geographical, cultural and economic characteristics of Alberta. Source themes explicitly include agricultural processing and manufacturing and service/recreational facilities, alongside administrative regions, agricultural production, natural resources, physical features and population. Those facility and industrial-processing themes establish the infrastructure component. The series is not updated and contains a range of publication dates; native time-span fields give 1970–1988. The source says it can be viewed, printed or plotted. Exact facility variables, map scales, dates and file formats are not stated in the description. Natural and demographic themes alone are not treated as infrastructure resources. Geographic coverage is within Alberta. Related map components retain their native catalogue identities. The native packages list Open Government Licence - Alberta and unrestricted access, but isopen is false. Actual file access and any cost are unverified. Distribution metadata mainly points to HTML/XML descriptive pages; these are not machine-readable infrastructure geometries. No map, PDF, image, archive or dataset body was fetched. Specific simulation uses are not stated.
